title: Evaluation of the OHLP of people with a migration background
summary:
Tooth decay in early childhood is widespread in Germany - every second child shows signs of tooth damage by the age of six. Children with a migration background are particularly affected. They show an above-average incidence of poor dental health, which can be attributed to poorer oral health knowledge, language barriers or a lower utilisation of preventive care services.
This study investigates whether targeted education of parents as part of the early dental check-up (FU1/FU2) can help to improve knowledge about dental health - so-called oral health literacy (OHL). The focus is on parents of children who have to be treated under general anaesthetic due to severe tooth decay.
To this end, parents complete an oral health literacy questionnaire (OHLP) before the first appointment and again six months later. The OHLPis available in several languages (German, English, Russian, Turkish and Arabic). It is also being investigated whether the use of interpreters or digital translation aids improves the impact of the information and whether this changes the families' aftercare behaviour.
In the long term, the results should help to organise dental care and education for families with a migration background in a more targeted and effective way.

interventions.name: Assessment of the Oral Health Literacy Profile (OHLP) of parents of children referred for dental treatment under general anaesthesia using the OHLP questionnaire. The families in the study group have a migration background.

Assessment of the Oral Health Literacy Profile (OHLP) of parents of children referred for dental treatment under general anaesthesia using the OHLP questionnaire. The families in the control group have no migration background.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Children with early childhood caries (ECC)
- Children with non-compliance for caries therapy under local anaesthesia
- Parents or legal guardians of the above-mentioned children - Children with early childhood caries (ECC)
Exclusion criteria:
- General illnesses
- Regular use of medication
